paragraphs.S20.C000.P000: Alice spent the evening of day nine in her room. Through the wall, she heard someone drop keys in the hall; it was Nick, not Damir. She read a few pages of a book and fell asleep without a conversation about the past. In the morning, Damir met her over breakfast and asked whether their arrangement still stood.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P001: “Yes. But I didn't promise to repeat your famous dinner.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P002: “I don't want to repeat it either,” he said. “Let's see what's in the shop.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P003: She knew his shopping list by heart: rice, tomatoes, familiar spices, an attempt to cook quickly what had once worked without a timer. Two years ago, exchanging a look by a shelf had been enough. Today the similarity was both a convenience and a trap.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P004: In the shop, Damir reached for the usual packet of grain, then stopped.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P005: “Do you actually want this?” he asked.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P006: “I want us to look at everything first.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P007: They found a small packet of pearl barley, local mushrooms, and fresh herbs. Damir suggested adding smoked fish, but Alice was not sure the combination would work. The shopkeeper helped them choose a milder flavour. While the man weighed the piece, Alice noticed a rack of local postcards by the till: on one, the fish looked so ceremonious it might have been elected mayor of the town. Damir saw what she was looking at and bought the postcard instead of another tin of spices.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P008: “Don't try to bribe me with fish,” Alice said.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P009: “I bought it for myself. I have an empty wall at home.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P010: She remembered the flat where there had once been no room for anything useless. She had not seen Damir's new address. He showed her a photograph of the wall—small, with a shelf for books and one crookedly nailed hook. Alice pointed out where the postcard would look worst. He said that was where he would hang it: in the morning it would be the first thing he saw. It was an absurd but entirely his own future detail, not addressed to her.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P011: The bag tore at the handle by the exit. Damir caught the barley; Alice caught the bunch of herbs. They crouched right by the door, sorting the groceries into two bags, and burst out laughing because each was clutching their own prize. The shopkeeper brought them a new bag. When they stood, Damir offered to carry the heavy things; Alice gave him the fish and kept the barley. On the way back, he admitted that for the first time in a long while he had bought food without a mental three-day plan.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P012: “You are a doctor,” Alice said. “How will you survive without a plan?”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P013: “Very professionally. I will panic on the inside.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P014: She laughed. She liked his ability to make something useful out of disorder. Once, she had mistaken it for a readiness to decide for her too. Now Damir asked more often, sometimes awkwardly, as if learning a new language halfway through a conversation.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P015: They went their separate ways until dinner. Alice finished a note about the group slowing down for someone else's pace; Damir bought bread and checked whether they had enough salt. At six, they took over the shared kitchen: Eric checked the route and talked on the phone by the entrance, while Nick returned from filming the harbour. One burner was free. The owner asked them to clear the sink by seven, when the next guests would arrive. Alice set a timer and handed Damir the board for the mushrooms.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P016: Damir cut the mushrooms too small. Alice reminded him they would shrink.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P017: “Right. You always...” he began, then stopped.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P019: “You always noticed it before I did.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P020: “I did. But you still cut them your way.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P021: He wanted to object. She saw it in the way his back straightened. Instead of objecting, Damir took another mushroom and cut it larger.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P022: “You're right here. I remembered that we cooked together. I didn't remember how much of it was your silence.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P023: Alice turned the spoon between her fingers. She did not want dinner to become a trial of the past; even less did she want to give way again for the sake of a pleasant evening.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P024: “I pretended it didn't matter to me too,” she said. “It was easier than arguing over every small thing.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P026: “Now it matters to me what's on the plate. And what you hear when I say that.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P027: Oil hissed in the pan. They returned to a recipe neither knew in advance. Alice added the herbs at the end, Damir tasted it, and admitted there should have been less fish. The dish was edible and unlike their old dinner. He suggested writing down the proportions; Alice said she would rather remember the mistake and the successful correction. Both options seemed reasonable to him, and he did not insist.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P028: When the timer rang, an older couple entered the kitchen with a pot and bread. They were looking for a free place for their food. Damir was about to move someone else's dishes, but Alice stopped him and asked the guests whether they needed the burner now. It turned out they only wanted to heat water. Alice cleared her half of the table; Damir moved their pan onto a trivet. The couple got the stove, and the two of them got ten minutes to taste dinner without hurrying. Damir quietly said that before, he would have considered this an interruption to their conversation. “And I would have stayed silent and been angry,” Alice replied. They finished the first serving while the neighbours' kettle hummed beside them.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P029: At the table, Damir said that over the past two years he had changed shifts and cities several times, and in one place had learned to eat dinner alone without turning on the television. Alice told him how, after the breakup, she had been afraid to return to certain songs, then one day heard a familiar melody in a stranger's café and felt nothing but hunger. He did not ask whether that meant she had forgotten him. She did not ask him for a list of regrets.
paragraphs.S20.C000.P030: “I liked that in Vík we talked about how we live now,” she said. “But today, when you started the sentence ‘you always’, I wanted to leave.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P031: “I noticed. Before, I would have asked you to stay at least until the conversation ended.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P033: “Dinner is over. You can leave. I want you to know that I like talking to you now. Not to the person you were then.”
paragraphs.S20.C000.P034: He folded his napkin, leaving her room to answer or stand. The owner looked in to remind them about the sink. Together they put away the dishes, made room for the neighbours at the tap, and returned to the table without the pan between them.

S20.C001.title: Choice S20-C1 — What will Alice do after dinner

S20.C002.title: A. Stay for tea and offer a new kiss

paragraphs.S20.C002.P000: “I'll stay for another cup,” Alice said. “And I want to kiss you. But that doesn't undo what we talked about.”
paragraphs.S20.C002.P001: Damir froze with a clean plate in his hands, set it down, and asked:
paragraphs.S20.C002.P004: He approached slowly. Their kiss was familiar only for the first few moments; then Alice stepped back and realised she could do this without an explanation. Damir poured the tea. They drank it at the table without calling the evening a return.

S20.C003.title: B. Stay for tea without touching

paragraphs.S20.C003.P000: “I'll stay for tea,” Alice said. “Nothing more for now.”
paragraphs.S20.C003.P002: Damir poured the water into the cups and, instead of sitting close, took the chair opposite. They argued about whether a dish could be called successful if no one could repeat it. Alice said it could. He wrote down only the ingredients, leaving the proportions blank. It was an exact description of what they had agreed to today.

S20.C004.title: C. Leave while keeping the conversation honest

paragraphs.S20.C004.P000: “I'm going to my room,” Alice said. “I need to sit with this conversation on my own.”
paragraphs.S20.C004.P002: “I am not promising to return to it tomorrow.”
paragraphs.S20.C004.P004: He held out the container with the food left over, but first asked whether she wanted it. Alice declined. Damir closed the lid and put the container in the shared fridge for everyone, without turning it into a message she would have to accept.

paragraphs.S20.C005.P000: Later, Alice saw a note on the kitchen board: “Pearl barley, mushrooms, too much fish—reduce.” The handwriting was Damir's. There was no name of hers and no promise of “like before.” She added in pencil: “Herbs at the end.” When he came for his jacket, he noticed the correction and smiled, but did not search the house for her.
paragraphs.S20.C005.P001: Before leaving on the morning of day eleven, they both stood by the open boot.

paragraphs.S20.C006.P000: Damir asked whether he could put her backpack beside his. “You can. Just don't turn it into a system,” Alice said. He smiled and left space between the bags for Nick's things. Yesterday's kiss was not repeated in front of the group.

paragraphs.S20.C007.P000: Damir handed her the corrected ingredient list. Alice saw that he had crossed out the extra fish himself. “For the next dinner?” she asked. “In case someone asks for the recipe,” he answered. She folded the page and put it in her notebook.

paragraphs.S20.C008.P000: Damir asked whether she was comfortable putting her backpack up herself. Alice nodded and lifted it. Damir held the boot open without returning to the evening's conversation. The food container stayed in the shared fridge for the others.

S20.C010.title: Choice S20-C2 — How will Alice suggest spending the remaining free time with Damir?

S20.C011.title: A. Shop together for the next breakfast

paragraphs.S20.C011.P000: Alice suggested that Damir choose food for everyone, but first ask the others what they wanted. He posted the list in the group chat. Nick replied with a photograph of an empty cup, so they had to decide only the question of coffee for themselves.

S20.C012.title: B. Walk to the water without talking about the past

paragraphs.S20.C012.P000: Alice asked Damir to walk with her to the waterfront. On the way, he showed her a funny sign he had noticed that morning. They talked about the town and the cold wind, not about what had been between them two years earlier.
